newsitem.title: RUSSIA: China president expected to visit Moscow in April.
newsitem.headline: China president expected to visit Moscow in April.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin expects Chinese President Jiang Zemin to visit Moscow in April, a presidential spokesman said on Friday.

Press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing that Yestsin hoped that Jiang, together with the leaders of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, would sign an accord reducing forces along their borders.

Yastrzhembsky announced the timing of Jiang's visit after a meeting earlier on Friday between Yeltsin and Chinese Premier Li Peng. "Invitations to the heads of the three states will be sent," he said.

China's official Xinhua news agency said earlier that China, Russia and three other former Soviet republics had reached agreement in Beijing on reducing forces along their 4,300-km (2,580-mile) common border after seven years of talks.

"We hope to sign the agreement on reducing armed forces along Russia's, Tajikistan's, Kyrgyzstan's and Kazakhstan's borders with China," Yastrzhembsky said. He gave no details about the timing or extent of troop reductions.

China and the former Soviet Union clashed along their border in the 1960s when the two nuclear powers were rivals for the leadership of the world communist movement. Disputes over border demarcation were for the most part resolved in 1991.
